title: The Nameless
description: A tragic, choice-driven megadungeon for Fate's Edge. A silent archive under municipal seal hides a penitential labyrinth: thirty floors, each a memory the Penitent Lich cannot let go of, each locked by a true name. You descend to hold him accountable — or to free him. This dungeon is deliberately too long, a parody of endless Gygaxian megadungeons, but the length is the point: you're meant to feel the weight of thirty floors of unspoken names. Run it as a one-shot (6-8 floors), a short arc (12-16 floors), or the full penitence (all 30).
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: The Penitent Lich
bestiary.description: Once mortal, now an anchor of memory. He refuses oblivion until every name he harmed is spoken correctly and set in its rightful place. He appears through most of the dungeon as an echo, a memory-mask, or a quiet voice narrating each floor's penance — not a monster to be fought. He only manifests physically, and violently, if the party initiates violence.

sb_spends.name: Circle of Woe
sb_spends.effect: AoE targeting all PCs, DV 4; deals Harm 1 and inflicts Condition: Shaken on failure/partial. Only available once the True Form Manifestation Timer has filled to 4.

sb_spends.name: Unmaking Word
sb_spends.effect: Target one PC, DV 5; Severe consequence (Incapacitation or Major Item Destruction). Only available once the True Form Manifestation Timer has filled to 6 — invoked once, without cost.

sb_spends.name: Memory Lash
sb_spends.effect: Forces a PC to confront a personal failure mid-fight; DV 3 Presence+Insight or gain Condition: Distracted.

bestiary.lore: The lich does not want to win a fight. He wants to be witnessed. Violence against him is treated narratively as tragedy, not triumph — see the Combat Timers (Lich's Phylactery Pulse [4], Lich's True Form Manifestation [6], Party Dissolution [4]) for how badly a violent approach goes for the party. GMs should telegraph, hard, that this path leads to swift and total defeat, and that the true challenge is moral and narrative, not martial.

acts.title: The Descent (Floors 1–10)
acts.description: The first ten floors of the Nameless — early grievances, workshop betrayals, wartime cruelties. Each floor is a self-contained penance: a memory, a name, a fork between mercy and cruelty.

scenes.title: Floor 1: The Abandoned Apprentice
scenes.description: He left his first student locked out of the rite to claim credit. The air crackles with stolen power as a chalk-circle splits the workshop in two. On one side, pristine tools await an absent master; on the other, scorch marks and scattered notes speak of a student who was never meant to return. Among the debris, fragments of Utaran law bear witness to forgotten obligations.

timers.name: Floor 1 Timer
timers.description: The circle erupts in wild energy, summoning additional constructs while the apprentice's notes begin to burn themselves unreadable. A fragment of Utaran law scrolls out, bearing regulations on proper master-apprentice relations that were ignored during the empire's final years.

encounters.name: Floor 1: The Abandoned Apprentice — Resolution Fork

outcomes.partial: A costly middle path: Stain - Unworthy Teacher if you erase records; Ledger - Helped: Gwen if you validate her. Mercy (validating the apprentice) raises Position next floor; cruelty (destroying evidence) drops it.
outcomes.miss: When the Floor Timer fills: The circle erupts in wild energy, summoning additional constructs while the apprentice's notes begin to burn themselves unreadable. A fragment of Utaran law scrolls out, bearing regulations on proper master-apprentice relations that were ignored during the empire's final years.

scenes.title: Floor 2: The Broken Vow
scenes.description: He abandoned his wedding mid-ritual for discovery. Frost-laced petals hang in the air, refusing to fall. The choir inhales a vow backward, their voices carrying the cadence of Utaran ceremonial traditions now lost to time.

timers.name: Floor 2 Timer

npcs.secret: He was a high official of the Utaran Empire during its final years — administrator, jurist, and eventually necromancer — whose 'petty jealousies,' unlawful executions, and forbidden necromancy in the census vaults during the Siege of Ecktoria contributed materially to the empire's collapse 300 years ago. notes:
This dungeon is deliberately too long — a parody of endless Gygaxian megadungeons where every hallway has a gelatinous cube and every door hides a save-or-die. But parody doesn't mean empty: the length is part of the penance. Run it as a one-shot (pick 6–8 floors), a short arc (12–16 floors), or the full penitence (all 30) — this JSON module includes all 30 floors as scenes across three Acts so a table can choose their own scope by simply skipping scenes; the GM is not obligated to run them in strict numeric order, though the source recommends it. The lich isn't 'defeated' — he's convinced.

Floor-as-Leg Procedure: treat each floor as a Travel 'leg.' Draw a seed (Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage) from a reskinned Dungeon Deck, or use the floor's own listed elements. Start each floor at Dominant Position and adjust for bold risks, insight, or backlash. Track the Floor Timer [4–6] — [4] for compact scenes, [5] for tense puzzles/social play, [6] for complex combats or multifaceted dilemmas. Prefer spending SB to reveal memory, raise stakes, or tilt loyalties over raw damage; draw from the Deck of Consequences when the scene earns it. Each floor ends on a Resolution Fork that reframes the lich and tunes Position for the next floor.

Deck Usage: Hearts — shame, love, vows, memory-ghosts. Clubs — breakage, traps, relentless pursuers. Diamonds — wards, keys, rights of passage, bargains. Spades — necromancy, omens, soul-anchors, whispers.

Tiering: Party Tier I–II — default timers [4–5], sparse reinforcements, SB favors revelations and single-issue conditions. Tier III+ — more [6] timers, layered wards, factional crossfire, and SB can call reinforcements, gear failure, or scene shifts in addition to revelations.

Tone & Safety: centralizes grief, broken vows, and contrition. Check lines/veils, use safety tools, and invite players to define what reconciliation looks like in this world.

The Penitent Lich is also a full Runekeeper Patron (Tenets, Devotions & Boons by Favor 0–5, a Runekeeper list, Rites & Invocations, Compels & Taboos, Offerings & Obligations) detailed in full in this adventure's HTML doc and in the source material (fates-edge-docs/ttrpg/reference/adventures/nameless.tex). If a PC wants to swear to him mid-dungeon, that's intended: Favor moves by naming the harmed, choosing restitution, keeping hard watches, and completing rites of remembrance, and drops by erasing names, refusing confession, or striking down a pleading foe without terms.

Combat is explicitly the losing path (see the Lich's Phylactery Pulse / True Form Manifestation / Party Dissolution campaign timers) — if players initiate violence, shift the scene to Desperate immediately and let them feel, fast, that this route leads to total defeat, not victory.

pacing.overview: Each floor is a complete penance loop: a memory-in-one-line, an entry read-aloud, a set of skill Handles, an SB Spend Menu, a hidden true Key Name (with a Gentle Nudge → Actionable Lead → Aha! Proof clue ladder), a Resolution Fork (Mercy / Restitution / Renunciation), and an exit beat. Speaking a floor's Key Name correctly is always the cleanest exit; combat or workarounds are possible but cost more downstream. Fold Utaran Empire motifs (river-stone masonry, the Noon Bell, laurel-circle crests, Tri-Mark script, ash-snow, unfinished mosaics) into 2-3 recurring details rather than all of them at once — recognition across floors is the payoff, and mercy/restoration should make the motifs more legible, not less.
pacing.scaling: If the group is breezing through, upgrade a Floor Timer [4] to [5], or add a Ward/Alert sub-timer keyed to that floor's trap.
pacing.position_drift: Mercy, confession, and restitution raise Position on the next floor; cruelty or evasion drop it. Keep a simple per-PC toggle.
pacing.sb_spend_menu: 1 SB: memory whispers, +1 Supply segment, or evidence goes missing. 2 SB: alarm raised, lose cover, a lesser guardian arrives, or a vow-echo asks a costly question. 3 SB: reinforcements, key gear breaks, or a rail-tick toward a larger tragedy. 4+ SB: a trap springs, authority/an omen arrives, or the scene shifts to a harsher truth.
pacing.boons_as_compassion: When players console, bury, confess, or repair, hand out Boons. Let them convert Boons to stabilize Position at moral cruxes.
pacing.deck_cadence: Aim for 1-2 Deck draws per session unless the table wants chaos. Translate results into fiction (omens, debts, vows) rather than just penalties.
pacing.prep_shortcuts: Make a Name Ledger (Harmed / Helped / Unresolved columns; move names as choices land). Keep a Shard Kit (mirror shard, ring, ledger scrap, bone-petal — physical tokens that move between floors to track themes). Sketch the lich in three moods (Proud, Weary, Resolved); check one at the end of each session and bring that mask to Floor 30.

npcSecrets.penitent-lich: He was a Utaran official — administrator, jurist, eventually necromancer — during the empire's final years. His worst decisions occurred during its decline: the Siege of Ecktoria, unlawful executions, forbidden necromancy in the census vaults, and emergency edicts that cost lives. The dungeon never incriminates him directly; it only suggests guilt through echoes of administration, funerary rites, silenced names, and half-erased decrees. GMs: imply, never accuse — no NPC ever says he destroyed the Empire. Players should infer it through abandoned tribunals, burnt ledgers, missing names, and unfinished mosaics.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: That the Penitent Lich was a Utaran official whose decisions during the Siege of Ecktoria contributed to the empire's collapse — this should be inferred through echoes across many floors, never stated outright by any NPC.

That combat with the Lich is a losing, tragic path (Phylactery Pulse / True Form Manifestation / Party Dissolution timers) — telegraph this hard through fiction and Position shifts the moment violence starts, but don't preface it with mechanical warnings before the fact.

The exact contents of Floor 30's Final Persuasion Timer thresholds and destinations — let the party discover Continue Penance / Find Peace / Join the Living as live options in the moment, shaped by their accumulated choices.
That 'Utaran' is the name of the fallen empire — never say the word aloud in-fiction; let players piece it together from the recurring motifs (Noon Bell, river-stone, laurel seals, Tri-Mark script).

tacticalHints.utaran_mechanical_hooks: Imperial Research: when a PC frames an action as late-Utaran scholarship and presents a relevant artifact (coin, seal-fragment, ledger scrap, river-stone chip), grant DV -1 or Position +1 for Insight/Evidence, once per floor. Mercy -> Clarity: a scene resolved via mercy, restraint, or civic restoration reveals a clearer Utaran clue. Utaran Tokens: 3 may be spent for +1 progress on the Final Persuasion Timer, or to ask 'What restitution would honor the fallen city?'
tacticalHints.combat_guidance: If players initiate violence: shift the scene's starting Position to Desperate immediately; introduce the Lich's Phylactery Pulse [4] and True Form Manifestation [6] timers visibly; advance them per the SB spend menu and direct harm; introduce Party Dissolution [4] as the party takes hits or fails rolls under pressure; describe the Lich's transformation and the environment's reaction as wrong, immense, and inevitable. The goal is for players to realize quickly that this path leads to swift, total defeat — reinforcing that the true challenge is moral and narrative, not martial.
tacticalHints.corruption_system: Optional Penitential Corruption system: PCs gain Minor Corruption for small cruelties (breaking the etiquette of remembrance, exploiting grief, petty desecrations) and Major Corruption for taboos (erasing a name, killing a pleading foe without terms, shattering a ward, stealing a ritual for profit, phylactery desecration without rites). Each roll adds +1 Corruption [0-6] first, then rolls d12 on Table A (minor) or Table B (major) — full tables live in this adventure's HTML doc. At Corruption 3+: choose a visible Mark; deception about your past suffers DV+1; you cannot exceed Favor 3 with the Penitent Lich until you reduce to <=2. At Corruption 6: you become an Oath-Bound Revenant (all violent actions start Desperate; a personal Haunt follows you) until cleansed. Cleansing: public confession + restitution (-1), burying the unburied / restoring a headstone or ledger page (-1), keeping a named vigil (-1), returning a stolen token (-1), restoring a lineage / undoing an erasure (-2), or The Thirty-Spoken (leader only, resets to 0).
tacticalHints.name_ledger: Keep three columns: Harmed / Helped / Unresolved. Moving names from Unresolved to Helped is how a Runekeeper (or the party generally) organically earns Favor and steers Floor 30's starting conditions.
tacticalHints.shard_kit: A physical prop kit (mirror shard, ring, ledger scrap, bone-petal) that should visibly move between floors — each floor's own Shard Kit note (see per-floor GM notes above) adds to it.
